day_shape: 61 items: Trump signs Graham Russia/Iran Sanctions Act, Washington Post says US Iran-war deaths exceed Pentagon count by at least four, Iran executes alleged Mossad spy Hussein Pedaran, CENTCOM reports 105 vessels redirected under Iran blockade, heavy Sacred Defence Week messaging from IRGC channels.

threads.label: US sanctions law and financial pressure
threads.summary: Trump signed the Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, extending existing sanctions on Tehran and expanding tariff and restriction authorities. Turkey's BDDK revoked the operating licence of Iranian lender Mellat Bank's Istanbul branch under its banking law.

threads.label: US casualties and cost of Iran war
threads.summary: The Washington Post, citing six US officials, reported Pentagon figures understate American military deaths in the Iran war by at least four, putting the toll at 22 or more. Iran International reported Democrats are attacking Trump over war costs ahead of the midterms; IRIB amplified the Post reporting and cited a Quincy Institute estimate of $5 billion per month.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz and Arabian Sea posture
threads.summary: CENTCOM said its forces have redirected 105 commercial vessels enforcing the US blockade against Iran, with USS Boxer conducting flight operations in the Arabian Sea. South Korea told Secretary Rubio it would contribute to restoring free passage through the Strait of Hormuz; Defa Press framed a strike on a US Saildrone vessel and PGSA insurance warnings as a new phase of Iranian power in the waterway.

threads.label: Espionage executions and post-war internal security
threads.summary: Iran executed Hussein Pedaran, convicted of passing information on Isfahan missile sites to Israel's Mossad, according to the judiciary. Defa Press said 159 US and Israeli officials — 92 Americans and 67 Israelis — have been indicted over the assassination of Iranian commanders; the IRGC also staged a Tehran parade of Basij and children two days after the January protest anniversary.

threads.label: Detained protesters and dissent
threads.summary: Iran International reported a 21-year-old taekwondo athlete shot by security forces during January protests died after around 30 operations. A separate report said a woman on death row over the January protests has been denied hospital treatment despite a prison doctor recommending an urgent MRI; unveiled women runners at a Tehran 10k race went viral.

threads.label: Sacred Defence Week messaging cycle
threads.summary: IRGC-linked Defa Press ran a sustained cycle on Sacred Defence Week 1405 under the slogan 'Labbaik Ya Khamenei', citing 46 memorials open to visitors and armed-forces equipment offered to filmmakers. IRIB amplified analyst Borzogar's claim that Iran's military approach has become 'preemptive and aggressive' and reported registration of 31 million people, 32% women, for the Janfada mobilisation.

threads.label: Iran diplomacy and post-war economy
threads.summary: Foreign Minister Araghchi spoke by phone with Pakistan's Ishaq Dar and, per Iran International, is on a second wartime Beijing visit coinciding with preparations for Xi–Trump talks. Iran International said Iran has lost about a third of pre-war gas production capacity heading into winter; IRIB cited a Washington Post analysis putting 17% of Qatar's LNG capacity offline after Ras Laffan damage.

events.summary_en: The Washington Post, citing six US officials, reported that the number of American military personnel killed in the war with Iran exceeds the public figures released by the US Department of Defence. Five of these officials stated that at least 22 US military personnel have been killed; that is, four more than the figure recorded in the Pentagon's public database, known as the Defence Casualty Analysis System (DCAS). The sixth official put the death toll at 23, stating that these individuals were killed from 28 February onwards, when the Trump administration, in cooperation with Israel, began war against Iran. events.title_en: Washington Post: War with Iran has not just shaken the oil market; it has simultaneously affected several major global markets
events.summary_en: Morgan Basilyan, writing an analysis for the Washington Post, stated that the consequences of war with Iran go beyond oil and have simultaneously affected several major global markets. Liquefied natural gas; one-fifth of global supply removed from reach: damage to two Ras Laffan units has taken 17 per cent of Qatar's LNG capacity offline and alongside the Hormuz disruption, approximately one-fifth of global LNG supply has been removed from reach. Helium and advanced industries: Qatar's helium exports have fallen by 14 per cent; a substance vital for MRI, semiconductors and aerospace industries. Aluminium prices have also reached the highest level in four years

events.title_en: Indictment issued for perpetrators of assassination of martyr leader and commanders
events.summary_en: Judiciary spokesperson Syed Ali Kazemi announced the issuance of indictments against 159 American and Zionist officials in the case of the assassination of martyr commanders. In the case of the assassination of the martyr leader and martyr commanders, 159 senior political and military officials from America and the Zionist regime are under investigation, comprising 92 Americans and 67 Israelis. Indictments have been issued for the accused and the file has been sent to court. For 19 martyr commanders a file was established and investigation was carried out and ultimately indictments were issued against 97 American and Zionist officials, comprising 74 Americans and 23 Israelis.

events.title_en: New figures on the costs the war with Iran has imposed on America; 5 billion dollars per month
events.summary_en: Ben Freeman, researcher at the Quincy Institute: Centcom recently released an estimate of the costs of war with Iran of 43.6 billion dollars. On Monday, the US Department of Defence Inspector General also released an estimate of costs that was 10 billion dollars less than this figure; with the difference being that the Inspector General's estimate covered two fewer months. The translation of these figures: the ongoing costs of war with Iran have been approximately 5 billion dollars per month; a figure much higher than what we have been told so far.

The unmanned vessel that the Revolutionary Guards struck is made by the American company Saildrone and is known by the same name. The unmanned 'Explorer' vessel is actually designed for missions in which manned ships cannot navigate safely; as mentioned, this vessel can operate continuously 24 hours and up to 365 consecutive days at sea without support vessels.

events.title_en: Director General of International Atomic Energy Agency as war criminal
